name: Netherlands

income_tax.summary: Box 1 income tax for 2026 is 8.10% to EUR 38,883, 37.56% to EUR 78,426 and 49.5% above; the first bracket also carries 27.65% national insurance premiums (AOW, Anw, Wlz), shown as social security here. Employee insurance premiums (WW, WIA) and the 6.10% income-related health levy are paid by the employer; the employee pays a nominal health premium of about EUR 1,900 a year to the insurer. General and labour tax credits reduce the bill but could not be verified.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed also pay the same 27.65% national insurance on profit up to EUR 38,883 and an income-related Zvw contribution of 4.85% (the 2026 'low' rate, maximum base EUR 79,409) plus the nominal health premium; the self-employed deduction (zelfstandigenaftrek) and SME profit exemption reduce taxable profit but 2026 amounts were not verified. The 4.85% rate is reported by Rendement.nl for employees/others without an employer levy, and is assumed to apply to the self-employed.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Rates shown for 8.10% exclude the 27.65% premiums, which sit in the social-security fields (combined first-bracket rate 35.75%). General tax credit and labour tax credit (arbeidskorting) are not modelled.

regimes.duration_note: Maximum 5 years from the first working day. Employer must file within 4 months of starting. 150 km rule: lived more than 150 km from the Dutch border for over 16 of the prior 24 months. Reduced norm EUR 36,497 for under-30s with a master's degree.
open_questions: Whether social security applies to the tax-free allowance was not stated on an opened page (the ruling is a tax matter; assumed unchanged).
27% from 2027: Loyens & Loeff described a bill; Business.gov.nl states it as law. The WNT cap above EUR 262,000 is the 2026 figure only.
Self-employed people cannot use the ruling (employed status required).
regimes.name: 30% ruling (expat scheme)
regimes.description: An employer can pay a recruited-from-abroad or transferred employee with scarce expertise up to 30% of wages tax-free in 2026 (2025 and 2026), based on wages up to the WNT cap of EUR 262,000. From 1 January 2027 the maximum falls to 27%: employees who first used the ruling in 2024 move to 27% from 2027 but keep the old salary norms; those starting in 2025 or later also get the higher norms from 2027 (EUR 50,436 general, subject to indexation). Employees who started before 2024 keep 30%. The Loyens & Loeff piece was written when the plan was a bill; Business.gov.nl now states the 27% as fact.

rent_1bed_monthly.description: Numbeo average monthly rent for a 1-bedroom city-centre apartment, Amsterdam; crowd-sourced, 1499 entries from 235 contributors in the past 12 months, last updated 11 October 2026. Unfurnished/furnished not distinguished. Numbeo gives only 1-bedroom and 3-bedroom figures, so no 2-bedroom value is recorded.

source.title: Cost of living in Amsterdam (rent prices)

rent_2bed_monthly.description: Investropa 2026 average monthly rent for a 2-bedroom apartment in Amsterdam, excluding utilities and service charges, assuming 70-80 m2; typical range EUR 2,250-3,200. Furnished status not stated. Benchmark estimate, not an official statistic.

costs.notes: Numbeo reports 3-bedroom city-centre EUR 3,519.44 as a cross-check; no 2-bedroom value. Check pass 2026-10-15: no reachable source for a 2-bedroom rent (see dossier change log).

residence_routes: EU/EEA and Swiss citizens have free movement. There is no digital nomad visa. Skilled non-EU employees use the highly skilled migrant or EU Blue Card route with an employer that is a recognised sponsor: 2026 thresholds are EUR 5,942 gross a month for HSM aged 30+ (EUR 4,357 under 30) and EUR 5,942 for the Blue Card. Self-employed non-EU nationals have separate routes (e.g. the DAFT treaty for US citizens) that were not verified here.
open_questions: Self-employed/DAFT route and absence of a nomad visa not verified from an IND page.
